clips.why: Hook: 'so what really matters is cost, since Anthropic is cheaper per token, right? Not quite.' API vs subscription split; OpenAI's revenue is mostly subscription and Anthropic's mostly API; payoff 308.2: subscriptions are metered by tokens, API by cost. 320.7 and 333.5 spell out the rolling window and 'user experience depends on how token-hungry the model is'. Opening line has a mild 'this' back-reference, but the question restates what it needs.

Labs subsidize token usage at their discretion; the real tension is who pays for inefficient tokens: API users pay directly, subscribers are insulated (361.2). 373.6 adds the conclusion that token efficiency hedges against falling prices.

also_ok.why: The Pareto frontier we don't look at is token efficiency: GPT-6 dominates token efficiency while Opus 5.5 wins on cost, a tension between cost- and token-efficient models. Partly chart reading and opens on 'But'.

negatives.why: Strong opening ('cost of intelligence dropping... but is it really?') that turns into reading the Pareto chart ('this dotted line here', 'as you can see').
3D cost/token/intelligence plot narrated from the screen.
GPT-6 Soul/Luna/Astra trajectories and intelligence-index numbers read off the plot.
Closing thesis that cheaper doesn't mean more efficient, immediately shown via quarter-by-quarter Pareto charts ('as you can see').
